topics.label: Introduction to cancer evolution and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the core themes of cancer evolution and establishes the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Clonal selection and epigenetic drivers in cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer progresses through Darwinian selection of advantageous somatic mutations and non-mutational epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Cell of origin and the cancer stem cell hierarchy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cancer stem cell model and investigate how differentiation hierarchy determines cellular susceptibility to malignant transformation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory promotion of tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how microenvironmental cues and inflammatory signals enable incipient and established tumor cells to proliferate and invade.

topics.label: Techniques for studying tumor evolution and spatial architecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the genomic, spatial omics, and computational technologies used to map cancer evolution and cellular interactions within tissues.

topics.label: Multifactorial synthesis of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesises the interdependent roles of genetic mutations, cell of origin, epigenetic state, and microenvironmental stimuli into a comprehensive evolutionary framework.

topics.label: Closing framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture presentation and previews the subsequent session on cancer therapy.
